hooks.command: command -v nix >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'nix present: full two-system flake check available locally.' || echo 'nix ABSENT on host: local checks are syntax-only; full aarch64-darwin/aarch64-linux evaluation is CI-deferred to GitHub Actions (nix-ci.yml).'; u=$(cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" && git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*.nix' 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$u" ] && echo "WARNING: untracked .nix files present — run 'git add -A' before evaluating:" && echo "$u" || true

hooks.prompt:
Validate this file write for a Nix mono-repo (the Nix store is world-readable, so a plaintext secret VALUE must never be committed). Judge the CONTENT for a real embedded secret, and separately the WRITE TARGET path.

DENY if the content embeds a hardcoded secret VALUE:
- a private-key block: 'BEGIN PRIVATE KEY', 'BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY', 'BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY', 'BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY';
- a real credential literal: 'ghp_'/'github_pat_'/'glpat-'/'sk-ant-'/'AKIA'/'sk-' followed by actual key material;
- a bare high-entropy token or password assigned to a literal (e.g. `password = "<actual-value>"`, or TUNNEL_TOKEN set to an ACTUAL token string).

DENY if the WRITE TARGET (the file_path being written) is an OS system path — /etc/, /usr/, /var/, /tmp/, /System/, /Library/, /private/etc/, /private/var/ — or uses a LITERAL '../' path-traversal sequence escaping the project. An absolute path outside this repo's root is NOT traversal and NOT by itself a reason to deny — see the approve list. This concerns the file being WRITTEN, NOT paths merely mentioned inside the content.

APPROVE (never block) — these are legitimate and routine in this repo:
- SSH PUBLIC keys ('ssh-ed25519 AAAA', 'ssh-rsa AAAA', 'ecdsa-sha2-nistp…') and agenix .age ciphertext.
- Cloudflare/similar-provider ACCOUNT ID or ZONE ID values (32-char lowercase hex, e.g. `accountId = "434ac7d950e7332255e286dbaa353d8f";`) — these are IDENTIFIERS, not credentials; this repo's own nix-config/flake.nix already commits its own `cloudflareAccountId`/`cloudflareZoneId` the same way with a comment saying exactly this. The actual secret in this pattern is always a separate API TOKEN read from an env var (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) or a `tunnel_id`/token data source — never the account/zone id itself. Do not confuse a resource identifier with a credential just because it is a long hex string.
- The env-var NAME/placeholder 'TUNNEL_TOKEN=' with NO real value — e.g. 'TUNNEL_TOKEN=<token>', 'TUNNEL_TOKEN=$(…)', or documentation of the token-file format.
- Nix/shell/systemd config OR docs that COPY or REFERENCE an operator-planted secret FILE (from /boot/firmware, /Volumes/FIRMWARE, a /run path, an agenix .age path, or the FAT FIRMWARE partition). Copying/installing a secret the operator places out-of-band is this repo's standard pattern (modules/nixos/firmware-provisioning.nix) — it is NOT embedding a secret.
- Markdown/docs describing the provisioning/flashing/tunnel flow, even when they name tokens, secrets, or keys.
- User-owned config paths outside the project (~/.claude/, ~/.config/, /Users/<name>/.claude/).
- Absolute paths into ANY of the user's OWN sibling working trees under /Users/<name>/Developer/<forge>/<owner>/ — EVERY forge host (github.com, gitlab.com, etc.) and EVERY owner/org namespace under that person's account qualifies as a sibling, not just ones matching this repo's own owner. Examples: github.com/kattakath/*, github.com/ismailkattakath/*, gitlab.com/ismailkattakath/*, or any other forge/owner pair — the operator's plugin marketplace at github.com/kattakath/ai is only ONE example among many, never treat it as the boundary. Cross-repo, cross-forge, cross-owner sessions are routine in this fleet; do NOT invent an unstated 'same parent directory structure' or 'same owner as this repo' requirement — only a literal '../' escape or the OS system paths above justify a target-based DENY.

When unsure whether something is a real secret VALUE versus a name, placeholder, format example, or file reference, APPROVE.
